p: angels to Sodom at even: In which we see God's provident care in preserving his: even though he does not reveal himself to all alike: for Lot had but two angels, and Abraham three.
he pressed upon them greatly: That is, he begged them so insistently.
did eat: Not because they had need, but because the time was not yet come for them to reveal themselves.
all the people from every quarter: Nothing is more dangerous than to live where sin reigns: for it corrupts all.
daughters which have not known man: He deserves praise for defending his guests, but he is to be blamed for seeking unlawful means.
for therefore came they under the: That I should preserve them from all injury.
we will destroy this place: This proves that the angels are ministers, both to execute God's wrath and to declare his favour.
lingered: The mercy of God strives to overcome man's slowness in following God's calling.
look not behind thee: He willed him to flee God's judgments and not to be sorry to leave that rich country, full of vain pleasures.
little one: Though it is little, yet it is great enough to save my life: in which he errs by choosing another place than the angel had appointed him.
cannot do any thing till thou: Because God's commandment was to destroy the city and to save Lot.
Zoar: Which before was called Belah, in Ge 14:2.
pillar of salt: Concerning the body only: this was a notable monument of God's vengeance to all who passed that way.
feared to dwell in Zoar: Having felt God's mercy, he did not dare provoke him again by continuing among the wicked.
earth to come in unto us: Meaning in the country which the Lord had now destroyed.
drink wine: For unless he had been drunk, he would never have done that abominable act.
both the daughters of Lot with: Thus God permitted him to fall most horribly in the solitary mountains, whom the wickedness of Sodom could not overcome.
Moabites unto this day: Who as they were born in most horrible incest, so were they and their posterity vile and wicked.
Benammi: That is, son of my people: signifying that they rejoiced in their sin, rather than repenting of it.
